questions.question: "quickly" can't be tested as written. What is the measurable version (a number, a time, a specific behaviour)?
questions.why: A test needs a threshold or a concrete expectation.
questions.quote: As a shopper, I want to place an order and get a confirmation quickly.

questions.question: Which status code and error body should this return (for example 400 or 422, and which message or error code)?
questions.why: A rejection test needs the exact status and body; "any 4xx" also passes when the request fails for the wrong reason, such as a typo in the URL.
questions.quote: An order that can't be fulfilled is rejected

questions.question: The story is for a shopper. What should happen without credentials, and when one user calls with another user's IDs: 401, 403 or 404?
questions.why: Access control is the API's job, not the UI's; without an expected answer a test can't tell a missing check from a correct one.

assumptions: The tests will use a shopper account.
Anything a question above asks about will be left as a TODO, not guessed.
